LESSON: TEMPERATURE

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.5 Time, Distance, and Speed (8 lessons) • Conversions in time • C
Topic 3.6: Temperature
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Temperature, part of Measurements 3.5 Time, Distance, and Speed (8 lessons) • Conversions in time • C in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How does temperature affect our everyday lives? 2. How do we measure temperature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the temperature conditions of the immediate environment as either warm, hot or cold

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. compare temperature using hotter, warmer, colder and same as in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. identify units of measuring temperature as degrees Celsius and Kelvin in different situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. convert units of measuring temperature from degree Celsius to Kelvin and vice- versa

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. work out temperature in degrees Celsius and Kelvin in real-life situations

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. use IT devices or other

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Temperature in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. move to the field, observe the temperature in the environment, and discuss the temperature conditions as either warm, hot or cold
2. discuss and test the temperature of different substances using arbitrary methods like touching, cold, warm, or hot water (exercise caution

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Temperature together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner works with peers and uses tools for measuring temperature.

● Digital Literacy: interacting with technology as the learner determines the temperature of different places using digital

devices.

Values

● Responsibility: as the learner handles tools of measuring temperature.

● Integrity: as the learner gives correct measurements of temperature.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Self-awareness: as the learner takes their body temperatures that is an indicator of health status.

● Safety: as the learner works together with others and exercises caution when dealing with hot substances.

Link to other Learning Areas:

● Integrated Science: as the learner considers their body temperatures to establish their health status and dress appropriately.

● Social studies: as the learner considers different climatic temperature changes.

Main points to remember:

1. describe the temperature conditions of the immediate environment as either warm, hot or cold
2. compare temperature using hotter, warmer, colder and same as in different situations
3. identify units of measuring temperature as degrees Celsius and Kelvin in different situations
4. convert units of measuring temperature from degree Celsius to Kelvin and vice- versa
5. work out temperature in degrees Celsius and Kelvin in real-life situations
6. use IT devices or other
